Tessa / Daniel — quick network-level notes after looking at the SVG and matrix: 

- Control-plane: make the control-plane endpoints single-homed to the management subnet with no internet gateway. Use private IPs and require mTLS for any registration or config pull. Add a dedicated NACL that is very restrictive (only control-plane CIDRs + monitored port ranges).
- Data-plane: the edge proxy fleet should live in private subnets with NAT for outward egress (for OS updates, etc.). Use internal ALBs (or cluster IP + nodeport) to balance to the GPU pool; avoid public-facing ELBs unless customer explicitly requires.
- Proxy pattern: prefer TLS termination + payload validation at the proxy layer for enterprise customers where PII/sensitive inputs are possible. For ultra-low-latency customers, pass-through TLS is acceptable if the proxy only performs connection multiplexing and minimal auth checks. Document the tradeoffs in the matrix (latency vs inspection).
- Flow logs: capture at VPC + ALB; ship to a central S3 bucket or to customer's SIEM with 90 days retention by default. Also enable ENI-level tagging to correlate instances to customer workloads for audits.

Markus — a note on HA: for cross-AZ resiliency ensure GPU pools are spread with cross-AZ failover, and the proxy autoscaler has a warm standby to prevent cold-start latency spikes.

Will prepare a short list of required firewall rules and sample iptables/SG entries for the runbook.
